hfaqs.a: No. Start with spoken Gujarati in Roman letters, and let the script come second. Learners who speak first stay motivated far longer than learners who drill letters for a month before saying a word.
hfaqs.q: Must I learn the Gujarati script before speaking?

hfaqs.a: નમસ્તે for respect, હા and ના, આભાર, માફ કરજો, સારું, and હું — I. With those seven you can open any interaction in Gujarat politely while your vocabulary grows underneath.
hfaqs.q: Which words should I learn in week one?

hfaqs.a: The murmured vowels, three-gender verbs — કરું છું, કરે છે — and the soft છ sound. Ten minutes of daily listening retunes your ears within weeks; the pronunciation page walks you through each one.
hfaqs.q: What is the hardest part of Gujarati?

how.d: Short, plain-English explanations — no grammar walls, no jargon without a translation.
Each phrase speaks in a native Gujarati voice. Slow it to 0.2× and repeat until it sticks.
Every topic ends in practice: quiz yourself, then review the words until they stay.

hub_lede: Free Gujarati lessons in plain English — say it right, hear every word spoken, and learn the culture behind the words.
lede: Free Gujarati lessons in plain English — greetings, alphabet, numbers, conversation and verbs, every word speakable.
title: Gujarati

topics.desc: નમસ્તે and beyond — greet Gujarat with warmth from your first word. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: નમસ્તે with folded hands — respectful everywhere, from Ahmedabad markets to village homes. Casual હેલો works with friends; નમસ્તે never fails.
faqs.q: How do I say hello respectfully?

faqs.a: તમે કેમ છો? (formal) or તું કેમ છે? (informal) — and answer હું મજામાં છું, આભાર (I'm fine, thanks). Health-questions open Gujarati hearts.
faqs.q: How do I ask how someone is?

faqs.a: શુભ સવાર (good morning), શુભ બપોર (good afternoon), શુભ સાંજ (good evening), શુભ રાત્રિ (good night). Time-greetings show care; use them generously.

topics.lede: નમસ્તે and beyond — greet Gujarat with warmth from your first word.
topics.note: A note on નમસ્તે. નમસ્તે (namaste — I bow to you) carries folded hands and genuine warmth — Gujarat's universal key. Say it to auto drivers, CEOs and grandmothers alike; the returned smile is guaranteed. Respect first, everything else follows.
paras: Greetings open every door: નમસ્તે (respectful hello), જય શ્રી કૃષ્ણ (devout hello), હેલો (casual hi). Fold your hands, say નમસ્તે, and Gujarat opens — bazaars, businesses, homes. One word, infinite welcome.

Health-questions show you care: તમે કેમ છો? (how are you, formal), હું મજામાં છું (I'm fine), અને તમે? (and you?). Gujarati small talk runs on genuine enquiry — ask properly, listen properly, belong quickly.

Time splits the day: શુભ સવાર (good morning), શુભ બપોર (good afternoon), શુભ સાંજ (good evening), શુભ રાત્રિ (good night). Morning greetings before noon, રાત્રિ only at parting — timing your શુભ shows cultural fluency.

Partings promise return: આવજો (goodbye, come again), ફરી મળીશું (we'll meet again), કાળજી રાખજો (take care). Gujaratis rarely say goodbye without a next meeting — આવજો assumes friendship continues. Say it warmly; mean it always.
topics.title: Saying hello the Gujarati way

topics.desc: Devanagari's headline-free cousin — vowels, consonants and barakshari, made friendly. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Close cousins — Gujarati script drops Devanagari's top headline bar and rounds the letters. Hindi readers recognise most shapes instantly.
The vowel-consonant grid: ક કા કિ કી કુ કૂ કે કૈ કો કૌ — every consonant marries every vowel in order. Master one row fully and the whole grid unlocks.
Vowels first: અ આ ઇ ઈ ઉ ઊ એ ઐ ઓ ઔ — then ક ખ ગ ઘ ચ છ જ ઝ. Sounds before shapes; reading follows speaking.

topics.lede: Devanagari's headline-free cousin — vowels, consonants and barakshari.

links.desc: Letters from zero, step by step.
links.label: Gujarati basics

topics.note: A note on the missing headline. Gujarati letters float free — no top bar links them, unlike Devanagari. ક ખ ગ ઘ stand separate and rounded. Writers lift the pen between letters; readers enjoy airy, open text. Freedom you can see.
paras: Vowels anchor everything: અ આ ઇ ઈ ઉ ઊ એ ઐ ઓ ઔ અં અઃ — thirteen pure sounds. Long-short pairs matter — ઇ vs ઈ changes meaning. Chant them in order daily; the mouth memorises what the ear repeats.

Consonants march in families: ક ખ ગ ઘ (throat), ચ છ જ ઝ (palate), ટ ઠ ડ ઢ (roof), ત થ દ ધ (teeth), પ ફ બ ભ (lips). Family by family, feel where each sound lives — Gujarati pronunciation is geography you can touch.
Special letters crown the set: ય ર લ વ શ ષ સ હ ળ ક્ષ જ્ઞ — with ળ (retroflex L) shared with Marathi. શાળા (school) shows ળ in action; જ્ઞાન (knowledge) shows જ્ઞ. Special letters, everyday words.

Barakshari grids it all: ક કા કિ કી કુ કૂ કે કૈ કો કૌ કં કઃ — each consonant through every vowel. One grid mastered teaches all grids. Read barakshari aloud for a month; Gujarati script becomes a friend for life.
topics.title: Gujarati alphabet

topics.desc: એક બે ત્રણ to સો — count, pay and bargain in Gujarati. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: એક બે ત્રણ ચાર પાંચ છ સાત આઠ નવ દસ — chant to ten, then અગિયાર બાર તેર ચૌદ પંદર to twenty. Rhythm first, precision follows.
વીસ (20), ત્રીસ (30), ચાળીસ (40), પચાસ (50) — then combine: એકવીસ (21), બત્રીસ (32). Tens plus units, endlessly.
સો (100), હજાર (1000), લાખ (100,000). કેટલા? (how many?) asks; numbers answer. Markets run on these three.

topics.lede: એક બે ત્રણ to સો — count, pay and bargain in Gujarati.
topics.note: A note on કેટલા? કેટલા? (ketlaa — how much / how many?) is Gujarat's most useful question — કેટલા રૂપિયા? (how many rupees?), કેટલા વાગ્યા? (what time is it?). One word, every transaction. Ask કેટલા fearlessly; numbers come to you.
paras: One to ten sings: એક બે ત્રણ ચાર પાંચ છ સાત આઠ નવ દસ — chant it walking, cooking, waiting. Gujarati numbers love rhythm; your tongue learns faster than your brain. Ten numbers, total freedom in every shop.
Teens climb steadily: અગિયાર બાર તેર ચૌદ પંદર સોળ સત્તર અઢાર ઓગણીસ વીસ — eleven to twenty. ઓગણીસ (19) and વીસ (20) open the tens; climb daily and teens become trivial.
Tens multiply power: વીસ ત્રીસ ચાળીસ પચાસ સાઠ સિત્તેર એંસી નેવું સો — 20 to 100. Combine freely: એકવીસ (21), પચ્ચીસ (25), સત્તાવીસ (27) — the tongue-twisters that prove fluency.
Hundreds rule markets: સો (100), બસો (200), હજાર (1000), લાખ (100,000). દોઢસો (150) and અઢીસો (250) charm shopkeepers — halves and quarters in pure Gujarati. Money talks; count it in Gujarati.
topics.title: Counting in Gujarati

topics.desc: હું, તમે, હા, ના — hold your first real Gujarati conversations. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: તમારું નામ શું? (what's your name?) — answer મારું નામ રાહુલ છે (my name is Rahul). Names first, friendship follows.
faqs.q: How do I ask someone's name?

faqs.a: હા (yes), ના (no) — short, clear, universal. જી adds respect; નહીં denies verbs. Yes-no fluency first.
મને સમજાયું નહીં (I didn't understand) and ધીમે બોલો (please speak slowly). Honesty tunes every speaker to your level.

topics.lede: હું, તમે, હા, ના — hold your first real Gujarati conversations.

links.desc: Dialogues with audio, step by step.
links.label: Gujarati conversation lessons

topics.note: A note on મને. મને (mane — to-me) is Gujarati's magic word — મને જોઈએ છે (I want), મને સમજાયું (I understood), મને ખબર છે (I know). Experiences flow TOWARD you in Gujarati; master મને and fifty sentences unlock.
paras: People anchor talk: હું (I), તમે (you formal), તે (he/she), તેઓ (they). હું ગુજરાતી શીખું છું (I'm learning Gujarati) — gender shows on verbs, proudly. Introduce yourself; conversations ignite.

Questions drive dialogue: શું? (what?), ક્યાં? (where?), ક્યારે? (when?), શા માટે? (why?), કેવી રીતે? (how?). તમે ક્યાં રહો છો? (where do you live?) — one question word plus any verb equals conversation.
Politeness oils everything: કૃપા કરીને (please) and માફ કરજો (sorry/excuse me). માફ કરજો, ધીમે બોલો (sorry, speak slowly) — apologies plus requests, the learner's armour.
Repair keeps talk alive: મને સમજાયું નહીં (I didn't understand), ફરી કહો (please say again), આનો અર્થ શું? (what does this mean?). Broken Gujarati beats silent perfection — stumble forward daily.
topics.title: Real Gujarati conversation

topics.desc: છે, જવું, કરવું — the verbs that carry every Gujarati sentence. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: હું છું (I am), તું છે, તે છે, અમે છીએ, તમે છો, તેઓ છે. Being first, everything else after.
Present simple uses root + છું/છે: હું કરું છું (I do), તે કરે છે (he/she does). The છું family carries the whole present tense.
faqs.q: How does the present tense work?

faqs.a: જવું (to go), આવવું (to come), કરવું (to do), ખાવું (to eat), બોલવું (to speak). Five verbs, half of daily speech.

topics.lede: છે, જવું, કરવું — the verbs that carry every Gujarati sentence.
topics.note: A note on છું/છે/છો. The છું family (chhun/chhe/chho) is Gujarati's heartbeat — હું છું (I am), તે છે (he/she is), તમે છો (you are). Every present-tense sentence pulses with છ. Learn this family cold; the whole tense follows.
paras: Being grounds all: છું/છે (am/is/are) — હું છું (I am), અમે છીએ (we are), તમે છો (you are), તેઓ છે (they are). છે anchors identity, place, state — હું અહીં છું (I'm here), હું મજામાં છું (I'm fine). Be first.

Going and coming move life: જવું (to go), આવવું (to come) — હું જાઉં છું (I go), હું આવું છું (I come). Direction verbs plus ક્યાં (where) navigate Gujarat — હું અમદાવાદ જાઉં છું (I'm going to Ahmedabad).
Doing and eating fill days: કરવું (to do), ખાવું (to eat), પીવું (to drink) — હું કામ કરું છું (I work), હું જમું છું (I eat a meal). Daily verbs, daily use; conjugate them in your sleep.
Speaking and knowing crown all: બોલવું (to speak), વાંચવું (to read), લખવું (to write) — હું ગુજરાતી બોલું છું (I speak Gujarati). Say it now, imperfectly; say it daily until the mirror agrees.
topics.title: Gujarati verbs

topics.desc: પાણી, ઘર, કામ, પ્રેમ — the hundred words Gujarati daily life runs on. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Body, home, food, people: પાણી (water), ઘર (house), મા (mother), મિત્ર (friend). Concrete nouns first — point, name, own.
Adjectives agree with gender: સારો (good-m), સારી (f), સારું (n). Learn triples together — agreement becomes music.
આજે (today), કાલે (tomorrow), ગઈકાલે (yesterday), હમણાં (now). Time words frame every plan — learn them this week.

topics.lede: પાણી, ઘર, કામ, પ્રેમ — the words Gujarati daily life runs on.

links.desc: Words in course order, with drills.
links.label: Gujarati vocabulary

topics.note: A note on સરસ. સરસ (saras — nice/great) is Gujarat's universal praise — સરસ છે (it's nice), ખૂબ સરસ (very nice). Food, films, friends' work — praise everything. Generous સરસ earns generous friendship.
paras: Survival nouns anchor reality: પાણી (water), ખાવાનું (food), ઘર (house), રસ્તો (road). Point at each, say it aloud, use it today — પાણી જોઈએ છે (I want water). Concrete first, abstract later.
People words warm speech: માણસ (person), મિત્ર (friend), મા (mother), બાળક (child). મારો મિત્ર (my friend) introduces proudly; મા calls home. People before things, always.
Describing words add colour: મોટું (big), નાનું (small), સારું (good), નવું (new). Adjectives dance with gender — મોટો ભાઈ (big brother), મોટી બહેન (big sister). Triple-learn each one.

Time and feeling complete the core: આજે (today), પ્રેમ (love), આનંદ (joy), કામ (work). આજે ઘણું કામ છે (there's lots of work today) — then પ્રેમ અને આનંદ balance it. Words for living, not just talking.
topics.title: Core Gujarati vocabulary

topics.desc: ઢોકળા to શીખંડ — order, eat and praise food in Gujarati. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: જમવાનું (meal), નાસ્તો (breakfast/snacks), ચા (tea). મને ભૂખ લાગી છે (I'm hungry) opens every food conversation.
faqs.q: How do I talk about meals?

faqs.a: આ શું છે? (what is this?) and મને ઢોકળા જોઈએ છે (I want dhokla). Point, ask, order — menus fear the curious.
તીખું (spicy), ગળ્યું (sweet), ખારું (salty), ખાટું (sour). ઓછું તીખું (less spicy) saves sensitive tongues.

topics.lede: ઢોકળા to શીખંડ — order, eat and praise food in Gujarati.
topics.note: A note on જમવાનું. જમવાનું (jamvaanun — meal/food) is sacred in Gujarat — જમ્યા? (have you eaten?) is love disguised as a question. Answer હા, જમ્યો (yes, done) and watch faces glow. Food is affection, served hot.
paras: Meals structure the day: નાસ્તો (breakfast), જમવાનું (lunch/dinner), ચા (tea). ચા પીશું? (shall we have tea?) — Gujarat runs on chai and conversation. Accept every cup; refuse nothing twice.

Ordering is easy bravery: મને એક ચા જોઈએ છે (I want one tea), બિલ આપો (please give the bill). એક પ્લેટ ઢોકળા આપો (give one plate of dhokla) — order Gujarat's soul in Gujarati. Vendors reward attempts with extra chutney.

Staples fill the thali: ભાત (rice), રોટલી (flatbread), દાળ (lentils), શાક (vegetables). શાક શું છે? (what's the vegetable dish?) — ask daily, eat variously. Thali eating teaches vocabulary with every bite.

Tastes tune the tongue: તીખું (spicy), ગળ્યું (sweet) — શીખંડ (sweet yogurt dessert) crowns feasts. ઓછું તીખું કરજો (make it less spicy) — then ખૂબ સરસ! (very nice!). Praise the cook; second helpings follow.
topics.title: Food phrases

topics.desc: Murmured vowels, soft છ, three genders of sound — speak Gujarati like a native. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: The retroflex flap: tongue curls back, flaps forward — બાળક (child), શાળા (school). Hindi speakers must learn it fresh; practise flapping daily.
Vowels half-swallowed mid-word — કહેવું sounds kahevun, soft and quick. Listen for the murmur; imitate the music.
Long-short pairs: ઇ/ઈ, ઉ/ઊ change words. Hold long vowels fully double — Gujarati ears measure length precisely.

topics.lede: Murmured vowels, soft છ, rhythm — speak Gujarati like a native.
topics.note: A note on ધીમે. ધીમે (dheeme — slowly) is the learner's best friend — ધીમે બોલો (please speak slowly). Say it with a smile and every Gujarati speaker shifts to teacher-mode. Slow speech is kind speech; ask for it freely.
paras: The signature ળ rules: બાળક (child), શાળા (school), કાળ (time) — tongue back, flap forward. Minimal pairs drill it: કાળ (time) vs કાલ (tomorrow). Master ળ and Gujaratis beam; skip it and they still understand, smiling.

Murmur runs through speech: કહેવું (to say), જવું (to go) — vowels soften mid-word, consonants relax. Gujarati sounds gentle because it IS gentle; harsh crispness marks the foreigner. Soften everything.
Length carries meaning: ઇ vs ઈ, ઉ vs ઊ — short and long are different letters, different words. Double the long ones fully; clip the short ones crisp. Ears measure; mouths must comply.

Rhythm ties it together: ધીમે (slowly) first, then natural speed; મોટેથી (loudly) for clarity, શાંત (quiet) for calm. ઉચ્ચાર (pronunciation) improves with echoing — shadow natives daily, record yourself weekly.
topics.title: Gujarati pronunciation

topics.desc: Three genders, postpositions, verb-final order — grammar without tears. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Masculine, feminine, neuter — nouns, adjectives AND verbs agree. સારો/સારી/સારું (good), જાઉં છું forms shift by gender in past tense. Triples everywhere; learn them as sets.
ને marks direction (અમદાવાદને — to Ahmedabad, rare), એ marks doers (રામે કર્યું — Ram did), સાથે means with. Postpositions follow nouns — learn each with ten examples.
Subject-Object-Verb: હું ભાત ખાઉં છું (I rice eat). Verb last, always. English order is the classic beginner error.

topics.lede: Three genders, postpositions, verb-final order — grammar without tears.
topics.note: A note on એ. એ (e) marks the doer in past tense — રામે કર્યું (Ram did), મેં ખાધું (I ate). Ergative, elegant, everywhere in stories. Tiny suffix, enormous workload.
paras: Three genders shape everything: masculine (છોકરો — boy), feminine (છોકરી — girl), neuter (બાળક — child, ઘર — house). Adjectives triple — સારો/સારી/સારું — and past verbs triple too. Gender is not decoration; it is Gujarati's skeleton.

Pronouns simplify persons: હું (I), તું (you-informal), તમે (you-formal), તે/તેઓ (he-she/they), અમે (we). અમે vs આપણે (exclusive vs inclusive we) — Gujarati distinguishes; English doesn't. Choose your we wisely.
Postpositions replace prepositions: -ને (to), -એ (by/doer), -સાથે (with-person), -માં (in). ઘરે જા (go home), ચમચીથી ખા (eat with a spoon). Suffixes after nouns — think backwards from English.

Verbs anchor sentences last: હું ભાત ખાઉં છું (I rice eat), તે શાળાએ જાય છે (she to-school goes). Present (ખાઉં છું), past (ખાધું), future (ખાઈશ) — tense on verbs, time words framing. Verb-final: the one rule that never breaks.
topics.title: Gujarati grammar, plainly explained
